Params: The test ends for now. Teddy says you can rest until your ride arrives. Just then, the sea breeze carries the distant noise of the festival toward you.
You can't see the crowd from here, but the bonfires and lanterns spill over like a warm river of light.
Vendors call out, people laugh, footsteps pass by, and machines hum in the distance. The sounds go on and on.
Not really. It's probably packed right now.
If we run into someone we know, we'll have to say hi and explain what we're doing.
You know I don't really like that.
Then what should we do now?
Rest time is for resting, obviously. I brought tea and a beach blanket.
Teddy is about to prepare for the next "mission" when a sweet, smoky smell drifts over. You aren't exactly hungry, but the scent is tempting enough to wake up an appetite.
I wonder what they're selling at the stalls.
Maybe. Want to check it out?
That smell is mostly nucleotide-based flavor compounds. My guess is grilled seafood... Oh, Commandant, want to play another game?
I'll admit, I'm tempted. But if I buy it myself, that would go against what I just said...
Right, Commandant. Want to play another game?
We already did a quiz. Let's play something else: rock-paper-scissors. One round. Loser goes to buy food.
Okay. I played scissors. I win.
You throw on Teddy's count and lose immediately.
Okay. I played rock. I win.
You throw on Teddy's count and lose immediately.
Okay. I played paper. I win.
You throw on Teddy's count and lose immediately.
We can play again, sure. But the famous Gray Raven Commandant wouldn't go back on a bet, would you?
I thought you'd fight it a little more. But a loss is a loss, so you're on food duty.
Since you lost, there's nothing to argue about. Teddy starts setting up a place for the two of you to rest, while you hurry off toward the festival.
Just as Teddy said, finding a seafood stall is easy, but getting through the crowd and into the line takes a while.
Still, you get the food in the end.
You're back. Your hair's all messy.
When you return to the beach with the grilled conch, Teddy has already spread the beach blanket beside the rocks. Two cups of herbal tea sit nearby.
Teddy pats the empty spot on the blanket, gesturing for you to sit down beside her.
Thanks. I thought this tea would go well with grilled seafood.
You and Teddy hand each other what you each prepared. As the tea and the bag of grilled conch change hands, Teddy tilts her head slightly.
It kind of feels like we're exchanging gifts.
Then should we thank each other?
...Thank you. Hm. Should I say it differently?
You're always so laid-back, aren't you?
The conch is still hot from the stall. With the tea, the sweet aftertaste doesn't weaken the seafood flavor. It blends with it, making the taste richer.
Before you can answer, Teddy leans back until her still-damp hair brushes your shoulder.
It is good, but... what are you doing?
The rocks are too hard... I thought I could use one as a backrest, but it just made my back go numb.
So in exchange for the tea, you're going to be my chair.
Wait, wasn't the tea for the grilled food?
That was what you owed me for losing. Don't mix them up.
Teddy leans back again. This time, she has you turn around too. After a little shifting, the two of you end up sitting back-to-back.
Commandant, I have a confession to make.
I've actually been testing the coating this whole time, right up to that rock-paper-scissors game.
We threw out our hands at the same time, but before you moved, the coating had already read enough signals to predict what you'd probably choose.
Before you can finish the question, the moment of first seeing Teddy on this beach comes back to mind.
Height, 20 meters. Confirming velocity vector, drag coefficient, and dynamic tracking accuracy...
Then Teddy caught the ball without taking even half a step.
Catching a ball, playing rock-paper-scissors... both can be calculated.
A coating can go that far?
You can go ahead and be impressed. After all, the reason I ran into you here is because this coating calculated it.
Of course not. I made that up.
Teddy puts a little more weight against your back.
Predicting someone's whole schedule would be Laplace's demon territory. Even with a bigger processor, I couldn't do that.
What I actually did was send drones ahead to see where you were going.
Once I knew your route, I picked a nice spot along the way and waited for you to find me.
Then maybe I'm Laplace's demon here.
Because while I was walking around...
I had a feeling I'd run into you.
Are you joking...? No, wait. You're serious?
The coating must have something like a lie detector. That's probably why Teddy stopped herself just now.
It wasn't a game. I used every bit of processing power to set that up, and somehow your gut feeling still beat me.
A soft warmth touches the commandant's lowered hand. Smaller fingers slip between the commandant's, fit into place, and hold on with strength.
This isn't a game to win or lose, but you still take her hand and hold on even tighter.
This is where you're supposed to say, "You caught me."
The sea breeze, the tide, and the distant noise of the festival drift slowly through the air.
You don't need to say anything. Sitting back-to-back, with your fingertips lightly touching hers, it almost feels as if you can hear her heartbeat—and she can hear yours.
Dusk sinks into the sea. The festival slowly quiets down, but you and Teddy remain on the beach.
Like two shells left on the shore, forgotten by the retreating tide.
For a moment, you think someone else might say that since you're here, you should get up and do something more memorable, something more meaningful.
But you don't want to. Neither does Teddy. Because when two people understand each other, simply sitting in the same place and sharing the same time—
